title: Wall mounted soap dispenser will not dispense soap; it went into the garbage
text:
Wall mounted soap dispenser will not dispense soap; it went into the garbage. About two years ago I ordered a $28 automatic soap dispenser. For weeks I tried to put up with it but It barely would dispense soap that I eventually threw it out. I had such a bad experience that it has taken me a couple of years before I decided to try this one that came up for review. After trying to get this to work for over 30 minutes, this also went into the garbage as per my experience below.

This is a wall-mounted dispenser. A key is needed to keep the top closed. Two keys, two mounting screws, and 3 extra nozzles come with this dispenser. It requires 4 AA batteries (NOT INCLUDED). The batteries get inserted in the back and there is an ON/OFF switch below the battery compartment. This means it has to be taken off the wall to change the batteries or turn the unit ON or OFF (should one be going away for a while and want it OFF).

I decided to test this before mounting to a wall and lucky I did. After inserting the batteries, I filled it partway, struggled to get the key lock to work to keep the lid closed, turned the unit ON in the back after inserting the batteries, and then engaged the unit. Since air can be in the line, I tried about 30 times to get the soap to dispense and nothing would come out. I even pulled out the nozzle and reinserted it. I had to pull out the nozzle with an open scissor because it was impossible to remove. The green foaming nozzle would not insert into the hole so I just reseated the one that came with it. At one point soap started to leak out of the seam in the back but it would never dispense it through the nozzle.

The instructions are not great but they are still somewhat understandable. After trying for over 30 minutes, I gave up. Besides not dispensing soap, the key lock is difficult to operate and very sticky and there does not seem to be any way to insert the green foaming nozzle if that is desired. The exit hole is just too small. However, these are moot points since after flushing all air from the lines, the soap would not dispense and then started to leak out of the seam in the back. It went right in the garbage.
